name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=chapter, descriptor=ch26_end_scene_char_pos_y_table. 'ch26' is the meaningful chapter ID (01-30 range, must be preserved -- not a Ghidra address residue). 'pos_y' correctly reflects per-character Y world-tile coordinates; 'table' reflects the array data type. No address residue. Name accurately describes the data and its type.
purpose: Per-character world-tile Y coordinate table for the Chapter 26 (未知的迴廊) end-scene cast placement.
logic_summary: 16-byte const table read only by fd2_chapter_26_end (@0x24E80). The Watcom prologue copies all 16 bytes onto stack scratch (4 dwords via MOVSD.REP at 0x24EA0-0x24EAE), then passes the buffer as the Y-position argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro, which indexes it by character slot (0..15). Sibling tables: X @0x522D6 (data_fd2_chapter_ch26_end_scene_char_pos_x_table), facing @0x522F6 (data_fd2_chapter_ch26_end_scene_char_facing_table). Contents: 06 09 06 09 09 0A 0A 0A 0B 0B 0B 0B 0B 0C 0C 0C.
element_semantics: Each byte is the starting world-tile Y coordinate for one character slot (slot index 0..15) when positioning the Chapter 26 end-scene cast.
notes: Reader fd2_chapter_26_end has zero game-side write-xrefs to this address (only READ/DATA from 0x24EAE/0x24EA9), so the table is genuinely read-only -> is_const=true; src already declares it const uint8[16]. Existing shared src comment block (chend2.c lines 571-578) is accurate/concise/ASCII final-state, covers all three sibling tables and the copy-as-4-dwords mechanism, so comment kept and src file left untouched. Ghidra data plate was blank (null) and was created with a concise symbol-level description (PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline). No logic issues; binary contents match src initializer exactly.
